explanation.en: A word that ends in a consonant joins the next one when it starts with a vowel: the consonant moves over, and the two sound like one word. Between two vowels, a light w or y slips in.
explanation.fa: وقتی واژه‌ای با صامت تمام می‌شود و واژهٔ بعدی با مصوت شروع می‌شود، آن صامت به واژهٔ بعدی می‌چسبد و دو واژه مثل یک واژه شنیده می‌شوند. میان دو مصوت هم صدای کوتاهی مثل w یا y می‌آید.

examples.text: Come on. Rise and shine.
Thank you. Oh, yeah, look at that.
I am Nick. I live next door.
Go away!

explanation.en: Small words such as to, for, of, and and can are said quickly and lightly when they aren't stressed: to sounds like tuh, for like fer, and like 'n'.
explanation.fa: واژه‌های کوچکی مثل to، for، of، and و can وقتی تأکید ندارند، سریع و کم‌رنگ گفته می‌شوند: to مثل tuh، for مثل fer و and مثل 'n' شنیده می‌شود.

examples.text: 'Do you have a bed for me?'
Fish and chips.
Can I help you?
I will go to the shoe shop.

explanation.en: Some common pairs are said as one short word: going to → gonna, want to → wanna, don't know → dunno. Films are full of them; formal writing keeps the words apart.
explanation.fa: بعضی جفت‌واژه‌های پرکاربرد مثل یک واژهٔ کوتاه گفته می‌شوند: going to می‌شود gonna، want to می‌شود wanna و don't know می‌شود dunno. فیلم‌ها پر از آن‌هاست، اما در نوشتهٔ رسمی واژه‌ها جدا نوشته می‌شوند.

examples.text: Oh, my goodness. What are we going to do?
I want to give you some money.
I don't know.
Oh, erm, let me see. It says...November 5th.

explanation.en: A t or d caught between two consonants is often not said at all: next door → nex door, just buy → jus buy.
explanation.fa: t یا d که میان دو صامت گیر افتاده باشد، اغلب اصلاً گفته نمی‌شود: next door می‌شود nex door و just buy می‌شود jus buy.

examples.text: I am Nick. I live next door.
Next time in Extra...
OK. I'll just buy the shirt.

explanation.en: A t, d, s or z before you or your melts with its y: would you → wudja, what you → whatcha, miss you → mishoo.
explanation.fa: t، d، s یا z پیش از you یا your با صدای y آن درمی‌آمیزد: would you می‌شود wudja، what you می‌شود whatcha و miss you می‌شود mishoo.

examples.text: Would you like a drink, Nick?
Annie, look, it's not what you write,
Did you hear something?
I miss you. The children miss you.

explanation.en: Inside a sentence, he, him, her, his and have lose their h, and the word joins the one before: tell her → tell-er, did he → di-dee.
explanation.fa: در میانهٔ جمله، he، him، her، his و have صدای h خود را از دست می‌دهند و به واژهٔ پیش از خود می‌چسبند: tell her می‌شود tell-er و did he می‌شود di-dee.

examples.text: But how did he guess?
That would have been my guess.
Give him a minute.

explanation.en: An -ing at the end of a word is often said -in', in quick and friendly speech: going → goin', something → somethin'.
explanation.fa: ‎-ing در پایان واژه، در گفتار سریع و خودمانی، اغلب ‎-in' گفته می‌شود: going می‌شود goin' و something می‌شود somethin'.

examples.text: I thought so! What on earth are you doing? Are you crazy?
Oh, well, keep going, Hector.
I've got something for you.

explanation.en: them shrinks to 'em and joins the word before it: tell them → tell-em, kill them → kill-em.
explanation.fa: them به ‎'em کوتاه می‌شود و به واژهٔ پیش از خود می‌چسبد: tell them می‌شود tell-em و kill them می‌شود kill-em.

examples.text: Tell them about the alternate version of you.
-Kill them! -Wait! Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa!

explanation.en: In American English, a t between two vowel sounds is a quick, soft d: water → wadder, a lot of → a lodda, got it → go-dit.
explanation.fa: در انگلیسی آمریکایی، t میان دو مصوت مثل d نرم و سریعی گفته می‌شود: water می‌شود wadder، a lot of می‌شود a lodda و got it می‌شود go-dit.

examples.text: Please, I don't have a lot of time.
-How is it out there? -It's a little nippy. Wear layers.
I think I got it!
Potassium. And some water.

explanation.en: In British English, a t before a consonant or a pause is often cut off with a short catch in the throat instead: not for you → no' for you, what's that → wha's tha'.
explanation.fa: در انگلیسی بریتانیایی، t پیش از صامت یا پیش از مکث اغلب گفته نمی‌شود و به‌جایش گلو برای لحظه‌ای بسته می‌شود: not for you می‌شود no' for you و what's that می‌شود wha's tha'.

examples.text: No, no, no, Hector, that's not for you.
What's that smell?
It's not a problem!

explanation.en: A sound changes to suit the next one: n before p, b or m becomes m (ten melons → tem melons), n before k or g becomes ng (in case → ing case), and d before b becomes b (good boy → goob boy).
explanation.fa: صدایی خود را به صدای بعدی نزدیک می‌کند: n پیش از p، b یا m به m تبدیل می‌شود (ten melons می‌شود tem melons)، n پیش از k یا g به ng (in case می‌شود ing case) و d پیش از b به b (good boy می‌شود goob boy).

examples.text: Oh, good boy!
Hector ordered ten melons instead of ten lemons.
We're gonna need some backup in case your bwood doesn't do the twick.
it can be avoided, it never has to happen.

explanation.en: In British English an r at the end of a word is silent, but it comes back when the next word starts with a vowel: where is → wair-riz, for a moment → fo-ra moment. Between two vowels, an r can even be added: law and order → law-rand order.
explanation.fa: در انگلیسی بریتانیایی، r پایان واژه گفته نمی‌شود، اما وقتی واژهٔ بعدی با مصوت شروع شود برمی‌گردد: where is می‌شود wair-riz و for a moment می‌شود fo-ra moment. میان دو مصوت حتی ممکن است r اضافه شود: law and order می‌شود law-rand order.

examples.text: Where is Charley? Charley!
Hector, please excuse me for a moment.
Law and order.
